cands.name: Rusty Glover

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican and former history teacher and coach at Mary G. Montgomery High School in Semmes for 25 years. He served in the Alabama House (District 102) from 2002 to 2006 and the Alabama Senate (District 34) from 2006 to 2018, including as Majority Whip. He ran for Lieutenant Governor in 2018 and State Auditor in 2022.

endorsements.text: Alabama Farmers Federation gave him an early endorsement in his 2026 Senate primary, according to Wikipedia.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or documented actions from Glover on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, or school choice. His campaign site pledges lower taxes and never voting for a tax increase, but says nothing specific about property or homestead taxes. We found no documented controversies about him. We also found no independent source confirming his claimed voting records on abortion and guns. His pre-2018 Senate bills and votes were not available in the pages we read beyond a few items in his Wikipedia entry.

qual.background: Served four years in the Alabama House and 12 years in the Alabama Senate, reaching Majority Whip by 2016, after a 25-year career as a high school history teacher and coach.
qual.why: Sixteen years of prior legislative service plus chamber leadership as Majority Whip put him in the high range for writing law and the state budget. His teaching career is unrelated to the job and adds nothing, and his committee seats were not counted.
